title: Can Oncology Workflows Run Without Human Touch? - Anant Shankhdhar, Risa Labs
talk_summary: Risa Labs built a four-agent oncology prior-authorization pipeline (eligibility, auth-status, medical-necessity, submission) and progressively removed human review by adding deterministic decision engines, multi-source evidence reconciliation, and confidence-scored escalation. Their core lesson is that LLM extraction alone is non-deterministic and cannot be blindly trusted, so they gate no-touch automation on corroborating evidence and route low-confidence cases to humans.

takeaways.what_they_do: A deterministic decision engine runs first on normalized data and flags/terminates cases that fail hard rules, so LLMs only handle what rules cannot decide.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also added a deterministic decision engine to flag the cases which would not move forward

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of trusting one LLM extraction, they require two independent sources (e.g., prior auth letters + portal data) to agree before declaring high confidence and skipping human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of just having one source, I have two sources that give me the same information and wherever they conquer, I can say with confidence

takeaways.what_they_do: The medical-necessity agent attaches a confidence score to every answer and only escalates low-confidence cases to a clinician, rather than reviewing everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: attaches confidence score to any answer. So, we escalate only the ones that actually need a clinician

takeaways.technique: LLM-generated tool/RPA configs from a reusable action library
takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain a repository of reusable actions and use an LLM to generate per-portal configs from it, instead of hand-building each integration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we made a huge repository of custom actions as well as popular actions... LLM-based config generation which performs these actions and builds the config

takeaways.what_they_do: A runtime self-healing loop detects when fragile RPA automations break during production and mitigates them automatically instead of failing the run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these automations are fragile, so it may happen that they break during the run time. For this, we have a self-healing loop

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than automating whole orders, they identify sub-cases (no-auth-required, already-authorized) that can be fully eliminated from human review, shrinking the human queue incrementally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we could eliminate certain orders completely from these two type of drugs... this enabled us no touch on a certain set of orders
